### Front line

According to the Ukrainian open-source mapping project DeepStateMap, Russian forces gained approximately 3.1 square kilometres of previously contested territory and an additional 3.6 square kilometres became contested, with Russian forces entering 26% of the village of Maiske in the Kramatorsk raion of Donetsk Oblast. No Ukrainian counter-advances were recorded. 

The Russian Ministry of Defence officially claimed that units of its "North" grouping captured the settlements of Barylivka in Sumy Oblast and Alisivka in Kharkiv Oblast; these claims remain unverified by independent sources. The Russian Ministry of Defence also reported offensive and artillery operations against Ukrainian drone teams and positions in the Kramatorsk direction and north of Dobropillya, as well as strikes in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast. 

*The Economist*’s satellite war-fire model detected 36 war-related fires over the reporting period, concentrated heavily in Luhansk Oblast (24), followed by Kharkiv (6), Donetsk (3), Dnipropetrovsk (2), and Chernihiv (1) oblasts.

### Strikes and losses

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed that its air-defence units intercepted a total of 621 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over Russian territory throughout the day—531 overnight across 12 regions and the Moscow area, and an additional 90 during daylight hours across seven regions. Independent geolocation project GeoConfirmed documented Ukrainian drone impact via footage showing a large smoke column at the Azot chemical plant in Novomoskovsk, Russia.

The Russian Ministry of Defence also asserted that its drone forces carried out strikes targeting Ukrainian energy and logistical infrastructure, claiming hits against a logistics centre in Kharkiv, two power substations in Volyn Oblast (Lutsk-Pivnichna and Kovel), and a dry-cargo vessel bound for the port of Chornomorsk. 

Regarding battlefield equipment and civil impacts, GeoConfirmed visually verified a destroyed Ukrainian MaxxPro armoured vehicle in Kharkiv Oblast. GeoConfirmed also documented Russian FPV drone strikes on civilian and medical assets, including an armoured SUV operated by the Ukrainian "White Angels" police evacuation unit, a civilian evacuation vehicle, two ambulances, and an agricultural tractor, leaving the driver injured. 

### Official statements

The Ukrainian Ministry of Defence stated that mobilized recruits hold official military status from the start of basic training and clarified that leaving training facilities constitutes unauthorized absence (AWOL). Ukrainian Defence Minister Yevhen Khmara reported speaking with Romanian Defence Minister Ştefan-Radu Oprea, discussing Black Sea security, Romanian pilot training, and Ukrainian requests for F-16 munitions, Patriot interceptors, HAWK and AIM-9 missiles, and joint drone manufacturing under the SAFE programme. The Ukrainian Ministry also highlighted battlefield testing of heavy casualty-evacuation drones and amphibious robotic ground systems, as well as digital food supply logistics.

The Russian Ministry of Defence announced that its nuclear-powered submarine *Generalissimus Suvorov* carried out a scheduled underwater test-launch of a *Bulava* intercontinental ballistic missile in the Sea of Okhotsk. Russian Deputy Defence Minister Vasily Osmakov also held bilateral talks on security cooperation with the Somali Defence Minister at the Russia–Africa summit.
